title: Write the threat model, now that there is no server to model
goal: Peer AI reports a threat model missing for the mvp stage. It was blocked on a question nobody could answer: what is the server. ADR-013 answered it by removing the server, so the surface is now small and nameable — the blob store, the recovery secret, an imported export file — and the model is writable rather than deferred again. Without it, the only record of what this design protects against is prose scattered through ADR-011 and ADR-013.
acceptance: Given the three surfaces ADR-013 leaves — the blob store, the recovery secret and an imported file — when the threat model is written, then each has its attackers, what they can see, what they can change, and what stops them

Given a found or stolen recovery secret, when the threat model is written, then it states exactly what the holder gets in each of ADR-013's three recovery modes, and what deleting the blob does and does not take back
Given an imported export file is untrusted input, when the threat model is written, then it names the abuse cases issue #106 records and says which are tested and which are not
Given rule 7 and ADR-011, when the threat model is written, then every clause is marked true, moot or still binding, with no clause left unaddressed
Given the model is written, when check_document runs against it, then it is ready, and docs/02-architecture.md's Risks section no longer says no threat model exists
